chunks: Abu al-Qasim Abdullah ibn Ahmad al-Faqih informed me, regarding what he authorized for me in Balkh, saying: Ali ibn Abdul Aziz informed us, saying: Amr ibn Awon narrated to us, saying: Khalaf ibn Abdullah informed us, from Abu Ishaq al-Shaybani, from Abdul Rahman ibn al-Aswad, from his father, from Aisha, who said:
Two prayers that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did not abandon, in private or in public: two units after the afternoon prayer and two units before the dawn prayer.
ai.seo_question: What are the two specific prayers the Prophet never abandoned?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration from Aisha (peace be upon her) to emphasize the consistency of the Prophet’s voluntary prayers, specifically the two rak'ahs after Asr and the two before Fajr, performed both in private and public. In Shia scholarship, this highlights the importance of maintaining regular sunnah prayers as a means of spiritual refinement and following the Prophet's exemplary practice (sunnah) in daily worship.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 2-105 Based on what the jurist Abul Qasim Abdullah ibn Ahmad related to me in Balkh, Ali ibn Abdul Aziz quoted that Amr ibn Oan narrated on the authority of Khalaf ibn Abdullah, on the authority of Abi Ishaq al-Sheibany, on the authority of Abdul Rahman ibn al-Aswad, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ayesha, “God’s Prophet (MGB)

never stopped saying two forms of prayers in public or in private : one was saying two units of prayers after the afternoon prayer, and the other one was saying two units of prayers before the morning prayer.”
